messages:
devsecops-bot: [ALERT] Suspicious SSO activity detected. 112 failed logins across 46 IPs in ~7m targeting admin group. Identical UA fingerprint observed: 'rwd-headless/1.2'. Possible credential-stuffing or botnet probe.

maria: seeing this in the audit stream too. Two admin accounts hit lockout thresholds, forced session revokes for them just now.

li: oncall here — collecting IP list and adding temporary WAF blocks. Also applying a short-term rate limit on SAML POSTs to reduce noise.

josh: do we need an emergency KMS rotation for any service keys? which service accounts could be affected if creds were exfiltrated?

maria: main concern is the CI service account keys (service-api-key-automation). Not seeing successful logins yet but rotating would be prudent after containment. Rotating SAML signing cert is heavier; avoid unless we see a successful auth.

karen: any user-facing impact so far?

maria: only the two admin lockouts — they were contacted and reauthed manually. No broad user prompts.

andre: I can add UA-based filtering to ingress to drop traffic with that exact fingerprint, but careful — some internal tooling also uses custom UAs. Will scope to high-confidence matches and blocked IPs.

li: audit query I ran: ```sql
SELECT timestamp, user, src_ip, user_agent
FROM sso_logs
WHERE user_agent ILIKE '%rwd-headless%'
  AND timestamp >= now() - interval '1 hour';
```

oncall-sre: blocked 46 IPs in WAF (rule id 9981). Applied rate-limit: /sso/saml POST -> 10 req/min per src. Pushed session revoke for the 2 admin users. Monitoring for 30m.

maria: containment checklist (short):
- block offending IP list in WAF (done)
- temporary SAML POST rate-limiting (done)
- force session revokes for impacted accounts (done)
- collect and preserve full auth logs for forensics (li)
- schedule KMS/service-key rotation (planned)
- update RBAC: remove admin scopes from any CI/service accounts where possible (josh)
- postmortem + alerts for UA-fingerprint spikes (maria/li)

li: filing an incident ticket and will escalate to P1 if we cross 200 attempts or see any successful admin login. Adding an alert for >50 failed attempts from distinct IPs in 10m.

josh: I'll start a PR to audit and tighten RBAC for 'ci-deploy' and other service accounts. If we can drop admin from CI it reduces blast radius.

maria: also adding an ingestion-time extractor to tag 'ua_fingerprint' for future detection and retention in audit logs.

andre: note — don't blanket-block UA substrings unless high confidence. Use combined signals: UA + IP reputation + rate. We'll implement a confidence score rule.

maria: agreed. Post-incident actions to own:
- eng-security: run timeline and postmortem (maria)
- infra: add persistent rate-limits on /sso/saml and WAF rules (li + oncall-sre)
- platform: add ua_fingerprint extraction and alerting (andre)
- eng: RBAC audit & PRs to remove admin from service accounts (josh)
- ops: schedule KMS rotation for service-api-key-automation and rotate if anything suspicious found (karen)

li: added checklist to incident ticket #INC-2026 and assigned tasks. Will update thread with forensic dump link once uploaded.

maria: thanks team. Keep updates here. If anyone sees a successful login from those IPs or a new UA variant, tag @maria and escalate. :eyes:
